solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The woman wants to change a line of family

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman
to edit a text is to change it
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A woman is keen to rewrite her family's line of descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' gives RY, the usual crossword abbreviation for a railway line, not a line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hereditary is passed down within a family, so it is an adjective meaning belonging to the family line.

clue.text: Very good and completely audible?

indicators.note: audible says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: wholly means completely

explanation.surface: Something is praised as excellent and perfectly heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly or virtuous, a description of morally very good people.

clue.text: Jazz artist with good voice, perhaps rising

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to voice is to emit a sound, one example of emitting

explanation.surface: A jazz musician with a fine singing voice is on the up.
explanation.definitionFit: An early style of syncopated piano music, a forerunner of jazz and often grouped with it.

clue.text: Corrupt editor stains paper

indicators.note: corrupt suggests the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest editor besmirches a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' looks like a newspaper but is an academic paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A long academic essay written for a degree, a scholarly paper.

clue.text: Wishing all the best for a criminal trap

parts.note: to can stand for for, as in a gift to you
a sting is a police operation to trap criminals

explanation.surface: Someone wishes good luck to a criminal setting a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising glasses to someone is to drink a toast, an expression of good wishes.

clue.text: Old colonialist offering extremely rough poetry

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, the first and last, of rough

parts.note: odes are poems, so poetry

explanation.surface: A colonial administrator writes crude verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Rhodes was a 19th-century British imperialist in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Rhodes was a leading figure of the British Empire in Africa, a colonialist of the past.

clue.text: Before discharge, name US drugs officer

indicators.note: before places the name letter ahead of the discharge in the answer

parts.note: an arc is an electrical discharge across a gap

explanation.surface: An American narcotics agent gives his name before being discharged from service.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a narcotics agent, a law enforcement officer working against drug dealing.

clue.text: A matter being discussed

parts.note: tissue is bodily matter, as in brain tissue or grey matter

explanation.surface: A point that is under debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A matter' looks like the definition, but 'matter' is body TISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the point under debate: the question at stake is the one being argued over.

clue.text: Like baby food and cold sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means the cold word encloses the food word

parts.note: chilly means cold
a dish is a serving of food

explanation.surface: A description of baby food and cold sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in an immature manner, like an infant, is an adverb of childish behaviour.

clue.text: On trial, so perhaps I will make laws

parts.note: in cricket the on side of the field is also called the leg side

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of trial and so may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone on trial boasts that perhaps they will be the one making the laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is LEG, from cricket, where the on side and leg side are the same half of the field; 'perhaps' rearranges TRIAL SO into ISLATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawmaker speaking in the first person: a member of a parliament is one who makes laws.

clue.text: A little farm in Ireland, very small

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small farm somewhere in Ireland is described as tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini is used as an adjective for something of reduced, very small size, as in a miniature version.

clue.text: Get on with it

parts.note: read as an urge to hurry, but to get on with people needs warmth and amiability, the quality meant by it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like an impatient command; read literally, 'it' is the quality that helps you get on with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiability or sociability is the quality that lets people get along well together.

clue.text: Acquire energy drink

parts.note: to win something is to acquire it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone picks up an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energy drink' reads as one product, but 'energy' gives E and 'drink' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is a common alcoholic beverage made from fermented grapes.

clue.text: Supposed to ride, he's unfit

indicators.note: unfit says the letters are not in proper shape and must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A rider is told he was meant to compete but is not fit enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to suppose or speculate, so the past tense matches the verb supposed.

clue.text: Perhaps Iran, supposedly holding old visitor in respect

indicators.note: holding means the respect word encloses the old visitor

parts.note: to rate someone is to respect them
a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: Iran is said to be detaining a former visitor regarding some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supposedly' marks the definition as one view: Iran has been called a pariah nation by some governments.
explanation.definitionFit: A term used by some Western governments for countries they regard as outlaws in international affairs.

clue.text: Obvious — only a suggestion

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
one can mean only, as in my one chance

explanation.surface: A remark claims something is plain to see, then backs off to call it merely a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implied hint or nuance accompanying the main meaning, a subtle suggestion.

clue.text: Football game finally finishes 1-1?

indicators.note: finally picks the end letter of the word finishes

parts.note: odds of one to one are called evens

explanation.surface: A football match ends in a one-all draw.
explanation.walkthrough: The score 1-1 is really betting odds: one-to-one odds are called evens. Sevens is seven-a-side rugby, rugby being a code of football.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a short form of rugby football played with seven players a side, so it is a football game.

clue.text: Marked card — ATM viciously swallows one

indicators.note: swallows means the jumble takes in the one
viciously suggests the letters of card and ATM are savaged into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cash machine ferociously eats a marked bank card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marked' looks like it describes the card but is the definition; 'viciously' scrambles the card and cash-machine letters to DRAMATC, and 'swallows' takes in the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic change is a striking or noticeable one, so the adjective means marked.

clue.text: Facing judge, regret being arrogant

parts.note: someone up before the judge is facing a court
pity is regret, as in what a pity

explanation.surface: A defendant before the judge is sorry for having been so haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up before the bench' is the idiom: to be UP is to be facing a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity is an informal adjective for someone self-important and presumptuous, acting above their station.

clue.text: Reward job in which DIY's botched

indicators.note: in which says the job goes around the botched letters

parts.note: a part is a role or job

indicators.note: botched means the letters are messed up and reordered

explanation.surface: A job where the do-it-yourself work went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reward' looks like a payment for the job, but it is the definition; 'botched' scrambles the home-repair letters and 'in which' sets them inside the job word.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally soil worth mining, figuratively a lucrative discovery or reward.

clue.text: Awfully riled up about fellow being arrogant

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the fellow
awfully suggests the letters of riled up are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A haughty man gets terribly worked up about a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges RILED UP to PRIDEUL, and 'about' puts it around F.
explanation.definitionFit: Prideful is an adjective describing someone full of pride, haughty and conceited.

clue.text: Lined up with independent film-maker

parts.note: soldiers fall in when lining up, so fell in is lined up

explanation.surface: Someone queued with an indie film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was an Italian director, a celebrated maker of films.

clue.text: 1 Down smoke on a cigar

parts.note: the exclamation formed from 1 Down and smoke is a cry of surprise, as is cor

explanation.surface: A smoker exclaims in surprise while puffing a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, like the one 1 Down and 'smoke' make.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a type of long straight-sided cigar.

clue.text: Cup made from it may sort of melt?

indicators.note: melt suggests the letters lose their shape and run into a different order

explanation.surface: A cup of foam plastic might partially melt under a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melt' rearranges MAY SORT OF; the definition is a description of the material, one used to make disposable cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Polystyrene foam, sold under this trade name, is the material of throwaway coffee cups.

clue.text: Lounge in hotel divided from its east wing

indicators.note: reading from the east side, the right-hand end, means the letters go backwards
in says the letters sit within the words hotel divided

explanation.surface: A hotel lounge has been partitioned off from the east wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds ELDI across hotel divided; 'from its east wing' reads it right to left, as east is on the right of a map.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to laze about doing nothing, which is a verb sense of being inactive.

clue.text: Bonus for a king

parts.note: per means for each, as in ten pence per item
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A payment made to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is a fringe benefit or extra on top of pay, a bonus.

clue.text: This could be major reversal for 6 Across's first letter

indicators.note: first letter takes the opening letter of the word Across
reversal says the number six is written backwards

parts.note: the number six spelt out

explanation.surface: A cross-reference instruction about reversing the start of another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 Across, but it is just the number SIX, turned round, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse has a major and minor axis, so an axis is something that could be called major.

clue.text: Follow round woman into tip

indicators.note: into says the round and the woman go inside the tip

parts.note: a tine is a pointed prong or tip of a fork or antler
O is round in shape
Ethel is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is followed round to a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform to the rules is the idiom's sense, so it means to follow orders or obey.

clue.text: Those finishing the soda admit gas is worrying

indicators.note: those finishing takes the closing letters of the next four words

explanation.surface: People who finish off the fizzy drink concede that the wind it brings is troubling.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic: what's eating you means what is bothering you, so eats is a verb for troubles.

clue.text: One taken out by striker gets banter during game?

indicators.note: during joins the banter to the game it happens in

parts.note: a match is a sporting game
stick is teasing or mockery, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: A football striker is substituted and gets teased during the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The striker is someone striking a light, not a footballer: a matchstick is taken out of the box to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker lighting a fire takes one small wooden stick from the box; that is the item described.
